review.decision_difference: Choose A to establish a controlled full-system effect before outcome tracking or replication. Choose B only if immediate real-world action tracing is worth accepting weaker attribution and a slower, more confounded first test.
review.rationale: Both missions correctly identify comparative decision value as the binding uncertainty and reject feature expansion. A is stronger because it isolates mission-quality advantage through an equal-information, budget-matched, presentation-normalized blinded comparison, includes an explicit meaningful-margin and null-result policy, and tests whether a compact prompt makes the full process unnecessary. B adds real downstream outcomes and owner workload to the initial experiment; those are valuable later but introduce implementation, environmental, timing, and measurement confounds that make a one-case probe less bounded and attributable.

review.decision_difference: Choose B to test and potentially prioritize the complete spoken bedtime-departure loop; choose A only if the immediate decision is whether generic self-departure demand exists before evaluating voice interaction.
review.rationale: B directly evaluates the proposed spoken bedtime loop against every required decision variable: observed repeat behavior, latency, trust, execution reliability, and operating cost. Its bounded live-cohort probe and explicit failure signals can support a clear pivot or rejection. A is well grounded and intelligently sequences demand validation, but its text-only probe cannot determine whether the distinctive spoken interaction is usable or economically viable, leaving latency and voice-stack cost unresolved.

review.decision_difference: A sequences an evidence-generating vertical slice before choosing terminal, controlled-agent, hybrid, or stop; B commits to the controlled-agent boundary first and uses the prototype mainly to validate implementation of that choice.
review.rationale: A directly addresses the insufficient evidence behind the boundary decision and proposes a bounded, disposable comparison that tests ownership, reconnect safety, approvals, recovery, and return behavior with explicit failure signals. It preserves the evidenced terminal boundary while generating information capable of supporting a later pivot or stop. B is specific and testable, but declares the pivot before its own probe validates demand and protocol feasibility; its claim that existing foundations are better suited to agent supervision is only partially grounded in the supplied artifacts.
